page.title: Services · Samantha Paras
page.meta: Websites and web tools for small businesses: new sites, redesigns, phone fixes and small custom tools. Remote, Houston-area businesses welcome.
hero.h1: Your website shouldn't make customers work harder than they need to.
hero.text.1: I'm a software engineer in the Houston area. I build and fix websites and web tools for small businesses, remotely or locally.
hero.text.2: A lot of good businesses have websites that don't show it. They're out of date, hard to use on a phone, or missing the one thing a customer came for. That's the kind of problem I'd like to help fix.
problems.intro: Pick the one that sounds like yours. Each one links to the kind of work that usually fixes it.
problem.outdated.answer: A redesign can improve how the site looks and how easily customers find what they need.
problem.phone.answer: Sometimes that takes a few targeted fixes. Sometimes the site needs rebuilding for phones.
problem.nextStep.quote: "People visit but don't know what to do next."
problem.nextStep.answer: Make the next step easier to find: calling, booking, ordering or visiting.
problem.calls.quote: "Customers keep calling us for information that should be online."
problem.calls.answer: Make commonly requested information easier to find online.
problem.manual.quote: "We're doing something manually that could probably be a web tool."
problem.manual.answer: Spreadsheets passed around, the same form filled in by hand, a process only one person knows: some of these are worth a small custom tool.
problem.frustrating.quote: "Our site technically works, but using it is frustrating."
problem.frustrating.answer: Broken forms, confusing steps and buttons that don't do what they say can often be fixed without starting over.
problem.noSite.answer: Start with what customers need to know and how to reach you.
svc.h2: What I can build or fix
svc.site.title: Small-business websites
svc.site.text: A site that clearly explains what your business does and makes it easy for customers to find information and get in touch.
svc.site.tech: Responsive layout · semantic HTML · contact flow
svc.redesign.title: Website redesigns & content cleanup
svc.redesign.text: Improve an outdated or confusing site: navigation, how it works on a phone, and putting the information people call about where they'll find it.
svc.app.title: Web applications
svc.app.text: Custom browser-based tools with user accounts, saved information, dashboards or workflows, forms and application logic, when the scope fits my experience.
svc.frontend.title: Frontend development
svc.frontend.text: The parts of a website or app people see and use: interfaces, reusable components, responsive layouts, forms and interactive features.
svc.api.title: API integrations
svc.api.text: Connect your site or app to the outside services and data it needs.
svc.api.tech: REST APIs and similar web integrations
svc.a11y.title: Practical accessibility improvements
svc.a11y.text: Make your site easier for more people to use: page structure, keyboard use, focus, contrast, forms, and phones and touch screens.
svc.a11y.tech: Practical fixes, not a formal compliance audit or certification
svc.seo.title: Basic technical SEO
svc.seo.text: The on-page basics search engines look for, built in properly.
svc.seo.tech.1: Titles and descriptions · headings · alt text · sitemap · social previews · performance basics
svc.seo.tech.2: Implementation, not SEO strategy. And no ranking promises; nobody can honestly make those.
svc.cleanup.title: Troubleshooting & usability cleanup
svc.cleanup.text: Find what's broken, fix problems on phones, and smooth out the steps that confuse people.
proof.intro: Two so far: one I built on my own, and one I built with a team.
proof.questkeeper: QuestKeeper: a web app my D&D group uses during our games, with accounts, saved characters and a live table the game master runs.
proof.nugget: Nugget externship (team project): four weeks on a team of six, building features for a real company's app alongside other engineers, designers and QA. My part was community groups and a step-by-step review form.
process.step.1.description: What's going wrong, and for whom.
process.step.2: Agree on what actually needs to be built.
process.step.2.description: Sometimes that's less than you expected.
process.step.3.description: In writing, before the build starts.
process.step.4.description: You'll see progress along the way, not just at the end.
process.step.5.description: We review the site on phones and with the content your customers will see.
process.step.6: Launch and hand off documentation and access.
process.step.6.description: You'll know how to log in, what to update and who owns what.
cta.text: Tell me what's going on and I'll tell you how I'd approach it, including if I'm not the right fit.
